rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for someone jealous or unwilling to share what they regard as theirs.

example.english: They are so possessive that even their girlfriend isn't allowed to chat with boys.
example.traditional: 佢咁佔有慾強，連女朋友同男仔傾偈都唔得。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 zim3 jau5 juk6 koeng4 lin4 neoi5 pang4 jau5 tung4 naam4 zai2 king1 gai2 dou1 m4 dak1

rows.note: Use this for the clingy, constantly-attached side of being possessive, especially in a relationship.

example.english: After we started dating, they became possessive and wanted to follow me everywhere.
example.traditional: 拍拖之後，佢變得好痴身，去邊都要跟住我。
example.jyutping: paak3 to1 zi1 hau6 keoi5 bin3 dak1 hou2 ci1 san1 heoi3 bin1 dou1 jiu3 gan1 zyu6 ngo5

rows.jyutping: so2 jau5 kyun4 fong1 min6 ge3
rows.note: Use this formal attributive phrase when the sense concerns ownership rights or possession as a legal concept.

example.english: This is an issue about possessive rights, not usage rights.
example.traditional: 呢個係所有權方面嘅問題，唔係使用權問題。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hai6 so2 jau5 kyun4 fong1 min6 ge3 man6 tai4 m4 hai6 si2 jung6 kyun4 man6 tai4
